definition: Coupled Pattern Learner (CPL) is a machine learning algorithm which couples the semi-supervised learning of categories and relations to forestall the problem of semantic drift associated with boot-strap learning methods..
details: Coupled Pattern Learner (CPL) is a machine learning algorithm which couples the semi-supervised learning of categories and relations to forestall the problem of semantic drift associated with boot-strap learning methods.

explainer.lead: Coupled Pattern Learner, or CPL, learns categories and relations together rather than letting each one grow on its own. This shared learning process is intended to stop bootstrapping from gradually wandering away from its original meanings, a problem called semantic drift.

tiers.eli5: Imagine learning what counts as an animal while also learning where animals live. Each kind of clue helps check the other, like two study partners correcting each other. This makes it harder for a small early mistake to snowball into nonsense.
tiers.practitioner: Use CPL as a joint semi-supervised bootstrapping process: candidate categories and relations are evaluated together instead of in independent loops. Seed quality and consistency matter because both parts build on early examples. Its central engineering concern is limiting semantic drift as newly learned material feeds back into later learning.
tiers.paperLevel: CPL couples semi-supervised learners for category predicates and relation predicates so that their bootstrap updates constrain one another. Its objective is to expand both forms of knowledge while reducing semantic drift relative to independently bootstrapped learners. The coupling addresses drift, but does not remove the dependence of bootstrapping on initial examples.

explainer.example: Suppose the seeds include “otter” as an Animal and (otter, river) for livesIn. New patterns may propose more animals and more livesIn pairs, with each learner providing context for the other. Coupling helps prevent a pattern that gradually collects unrelated entities from driving the category ever farther from its original meaning.
explainer.goal: Expand knowledge of categories and relations through semi-supervised bootstrapping while reducing semantic drift.
steps: Start with seed category and relation examples.
Learn candidate patterns from those examples.
Use the patterns to propose new instances.
Check category and relation learning against each other.
tradeoffs: Coupling targets the semantic drift of independent bootstrapping.
Joint learning requires coordination between category and relation learners.
Poor or inconsistent seeds can still mislead both learners.
